lines: When changing an interface, update its controller contract and consumers, then run `python scripts/export_contract.py` to regenerate OpenAPI. Keep example payloads synthetic and valid. Coordinate shared schemas and route changes through the integration module described in [Agent development](AGENT_DEVELOPMENT.md).
Current paths, schemas and behavior are derived from Pawse's code. Proposed interfaces are implementation agreements to review and test before enabling their UI.
+- [React agent integration and evaluation](WEB_AGENT_INTEGRATION.md) — actual routes, consent, evidence and verification boundaries.
- Imported device/report services, live video ingestion, full desktop-width QA beyond the rehearsal and public multi-user deployment have not been validated in this iteration.
`gemini-2.5-flash` appeared in the model listing but returned HTTP 404 for generation in this project. Credentials and recordings are not included in test fixtures or publication artifacts.

+The merged teammate React frontend was integrated on top of `dd99088`. After rebasing onto the teammate’s Gradium whole-call update (#42), the local check passed 86 backend tests plus all six frontend check scripts; production compilation passed. New checks cover handoff consent, four language codes, binary audio/error propagation, backend ranking preservation and service-worker exclusion of private API responses. Real local HTTP checks exercised workflow traces, demo policy citations and missing-provider/voice-profile errors without paid provider calls. Browser verification at `/app/?live=1` covered the consent gate, typed concern, care result, insurer preparation and rendered policy excerpts with source IDs/hashes and `insurance_approval: not_obtained`; console error list was empty.

+This is not a claim that PR #29's unmerged browser suite passes. No real microphone recording, EN/ZH/DE/HI speech accuracy benchmark, Gradium cloning or telephone transport was verified. React dialogue remains turn-based REST, not Gemini Live streaming. OSM remains an offline staging dataset. See [integration and evaluation boundaries](WEB_AGENT_INTEGRATION.md).
| `GET /voice/localizations/current` | Current session | Candidate readiness from Gradium |
| `POST /voice/preview` | Gradium consent | Short German WAV preview |
| `POST /voice/localizations/current/save` | Gradium consent, `listened_to_preview: true` | Permanent German voice ID |
-| `POST /voice/speech` | German text, `voice: my_voice/standard`, Gradium consent | WAV bytes |
+| `POST /voice/speech` | German text, `voice: my_voice/standard`, Gradium consent, optional `call_id` | WAV bytes + `X-Pawse-Call-Id` header |
| `DELETE /voice/profile` | Current session | Deletes only voices/candidates created by this session |
| `GET /demo/mimi` | None | Fictional six-scene rehearsal, scripts, cost estimates, claim checklist |

Audio input is limited to 3 MB, 0.5–60 seconds, mono 16-bit PCM WAV at 8–48 kHz. Clone input must be 10–30 seconds. The browser converts recorded audio locally before upload. Gemini requests time out after 40 seconds and Gradium requests after 45 seconds. One voice operation can run per session, up to five globally.

-Each generated audio file begins with an AI-assistant disclosure. The app does not represent the cloned voice as the owner speaking live. Transcripts and translations are drafts to review, not verified clinical facts or insurance decisions.

+The first audio line of every call begins with an AI-assistant disclosure. A call is a sequence of `/voice/speech` lines: the first response carries a server-issued `X-Pawse-Call-Id`, and later lines that send it back (same browser session, within 30 minutes) are spoken as is, so the whole call keeps one Gradium voice without repeating the greeting. A missing, unknown, expired or other-session id always gets the disclosure again; an id is only remembered after its disclosed audio was produced. The app does not represent the cloned voice as the owner speaking live. Transcripts and translations are drafts to review, not verified clinical facts or insurance decisions.
+# React frontend and backend agent integration

+Checked on 10 October 2026. The React app lives in `web/`. Build with `npm ci --prefix web && npm run build --prefix web`, then start FastAPI. Open `/app/?live=1` for backend tools or `/app/?demo=1` for the simulated rehearsal. Vite development uses the configured `/api` proxy. Credentials remain server-side.
+| Frontend role | Actual endpoint | Result and boundary |
+| Voice input | `POST /api/v1/voice/transcriptions` | Browser recordings converted to mono WAV; Gemini transcription. Microphone starts only after the owner enables it. |

+| Care / vision / orchestration | `POST /api/v1/agents/runs` | `{care: CareRequest}`; consumes nested `care`, `trace`, `actions`. Text and selected photos require Gemini consent. Video stays local. |
+| Vet discovery | `POST /api/v1/care/requests` | Generic veterinary query, location consent, no symptoms and no AI consent. Preserve backend ranking, unknown hours, source and retrieval time. |
+| Communication | `POST /api/v1/voice/scripts` | Owner-reviewed facts, separate consent, German draft with EN/ZH/DE/HI subtitles. No recipient replies or bookings. |
+| Policy evidence | `POST /api/v1/knowledge/search` | Explicit demo-policy panel; English lexical search and original citations. No private-policy ingestion or coverage approval. |

+| Speech | `POST /api/v1/voice/speech` | Reviewed draft, separate Gradium consent, selected approved own voice or explicitly selected standard voice. Binary WAV with playback/download; no silent fallback. |
+| Voice enrollment | Existing `/` voice interface | Same-origin browser session; existing clone/localization/preview/save lifecycle. |

+The new live handoff uses `LiveHandoff.jsx` and `agents/handoff.js`. It bypasses the older story-backed `livePhoneAgent.js`; the explicit “Open simulated Mimi phone rehearsal” button opens that helper with Gradium sharing initially off. The owner can then enable the teammate’s whole-call Gradium rehearsal. All recipient replies/results remain simulated. Mock phone agents remain rehearsal-only. A validated `tel:` link opens the owner's dialer; audio is not injected into calls.

+The language selector offers EN/ZH/DE/HI. German and Hindi use English UI labels where translations are not supplied; their API language and subtitle codes are preserved. Current conversation audio is turn-based transcription and browser speech, not a Gemini Live WebSocket session. No claim of real-time Live integration is made for this React client.
+- `PYTHON=.venv/bin/python bash scripts/check.sh`: safety, skill catalog, JavaScript, all `web/scripts/check-*.mjs`, OpenAPI consistency, backend pytest.
+- `npm run check --prefix web`: mock story contracts, clinic mapping, voice workflow, legacy rehearsal helper, real handoff consent/languages/errors, service-worker private-response exclusion.

+- A bounded actual-HTTP smoke check against a local server without credentials verified seven-role workflow traces, local policy citations, explicit missing clinic configuration, missing Gemini and unconfigured own-voice errors. No paid provider calls occurred.
+- Browser walkthrough verified the React consent gate, typed care request, agent result entry and separate insurer preparation page. See `VALIDATION.md` for the final observed browser result.

+There is no independent evaluation agent in this repository. Open PR #29 contains proposed browser/audio tests for older test hooks; it has not been merged or claimed green here. Real microphone capture, speech accuracy (EN/ZH/DE/HI), Gemini Live streaming, Gradium clone quality and actual telephony are separate evaluations. They cannot be established by mocked contract checks or a successful build.

+The OSM crawling snapshot remains an offline staging dataset under the crawling contract. It is not relabelled as a live provider or silently shown as verified clinics. With no Places key or external clinic backend, the React page displays a configuration/unavailability error. Integrating OSM requires an explicit provider/schema change and reviewed cat-clinic evidence.
+The service worker caches only the app shell/assets, not API responses, query URLs or no-store responses. Old Pawse shell caches are cleared on activation.

[PR #29](https://github.com/yyyuanfish/pawse/pull/29) defines a tests-first frontend contract, not a completed browser implementation. Its proposed `data-testid` hooks include `language`, `consent-gemini`, `record`, `audio-upload`, `audio-preview`, `transcribe`, `voice-status`, `message-input`, `talk`, `end-talk`, `cat`, `transcript`, `tool-chip`, `confirm-call`, `results`, `demo` and `simulated-label`. Read its full [pinned contract](https://github.com/yyyuanfish/pawse/blob/f08c1c40e3e4588ca32a70edfc930166e56bf11b/tests/e2e/README.md) when implementing the new UI; do not add hooks to unrelated existing elements merely to claim compliance.

Acceptance requires actual mic cleanup, mono PCM16 WAV conversion, safe transcript rendering, interrupted Live playback and confirmed dialer handoff. The proposed layout checks use 1280, 1440, 1920 and 390 px. Real-speech WER/CER thresholds in that PR are evaluation targets, not measured recognition accuracy. Browser tests are opt-in and must be run explicitly after integration; a green default backend suite does not prove them green.

+The additional `web/` client is served at `/app/` after building. Its backend mode, endpoint mapping, consent gates and evaluation scope are described in [React agent integration](WEB_AGENT_INTEGRATION.md). The original root interface remains available for voice enrollment.
